blocks.text:
Jason Myers
Chief Operating Officer
Roach, Moss and Hall
Dear Jason,

Thank you for entrusting us with the search for your next Chief Financial Officer. This letter sets out the terms on which we will conduct that search for {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}, and it records in writing what we discussed when we last met. We take a retained mandate as a partnership, and we like to begin with everything stated plainly between us. Please read what follows. If any part of it does not match your understanding, call me before you sign.
The Search We Will Run

You are looking for a Chief Financial Officer who can carry the finance function of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} through its next stage of growth. Our work is to find that person, to test them thoroughly, and to bring you a short slate you can act on with confidence. We conduct the search on a retained basis. That means we work only for you on this mandate and give it our full attention until the seat is filled. Discretion runs through everything we do. We describe prospective candidates to you by their current role and record rather than by name, and we hold names in confidence until both sides are ready to meet.
In practice the assignment moves through a handful of clear stages, and I want you to know the shape of it from the start.

items: We agree the position specification with you and your board, so that we are all searching for the same person.
We map the market, build a long list from that map, and approach prospects with care and discretion.
We interview and assess in depth, then bring you a short slate described by fit and evidence, not by name alone.
We stay with you through client interviews, references, and the offer, and we do not step back until your new Chief Financial Officer has accepted and started.

blocks.text: The People on Your Account

I will oversee the engagement personally and remain your point of contact whenever you want one. Sandra Fuentes, a Principal in our search practice, will lead the assignment day to day and own the relationship with you and with every candidate she brings forward. James Grant, one of our senior consultants, will work the market at the most senior level and lend his judgment on the finalists. Jeffrey Patterson, our research consultant, keeps the search moving and will be the one who confirms schedules and closes the small loops, so that nothing goes quiet on you. You will find us easy to reach.
Our Fee and When We Begin

For a retained search of this kind we work to a fixed professional fee of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.fee}}, which covers the assignment in full from the specification through to a completed placement. The fee is not tied to the candidate's eventual compensation. You know the cost of the search at the outset, and it does not move as the search does. We are ready to begin on {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}}, once this letter is signed and returned, and we will hold that date for you.
Fees and Payment

We bill the fixed fee in three stages tied to the milestones of the assignment: at your signing of this letter, at the delivery of the short slate, and on your chosen candidate's acceptance of an offer. Invoices are payable on receipt. Reasonable direct expenses that we arrange at your request, such as candidate travel, are billed at cost and set out in full, and we will clear anything out of the ordinary with you before we commit to it.
Term and Ending the Engagement

The engagement runs from the date you sign until the search is completed and our final invoice is settled. Either of us may end it earlier, in writing, and we ask for the courtesy of a short conversation first so that nothing ends on a misunderstanding. If you close the search early for a reason unrelated to our work, we will bill for the stage in progress and no further. If a Chief Financial Officer we place leaves you within the first year for reasons within our control, we will reopen the search once at no additional fee.
Confidentiality

We treat what you share with us, and everything we learn in the course of the search, as confidential, and we use it only for this assignment. Within our office, access is limited to the people named above and to those whose work on the search requires it. We extend the same discretion to candidates. We do not disclose a prospect's interest to anyone outside your committee without their knowledge, and we describe them by their role rather than their name until you are ready to meet. Discretion is not a courtesy in our work. It is the condition that lets good people talk to us at all.
Limitation of Liability

We give this search our best professional judgment, but the choice of whom to hire is finally yours, and we cannot warrant the future performance of any person you appoint. Our liability to you arising out of this engagement, whether framed in contract or in negligence, will not exceed the total fees you pay us under it, save in the case of our own fraud or willful misconduct. Neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our office sits, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Should a dispute arise, we will each make a genuine effort to settle it in conversation before either of us turns to any other forum.

If these terms read as we agreed, please sign both copies where indicated below, keep one for your file, and return the other to me. That single step is all we need to begin. If anything here gives you pause, call me first and we will settle it before you sign. We are glad to be doing this with you.
With warm regards,
Kickoff Memo: CFO Search for Roach, Moss and Hall

To: Jeffrey Patterson; James Grant
From: Sandra Fuentes
Re: How we will run the CFO search

Our job on this one is simple to state and hard to do well: put a Chief Financial Officer in front of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} whom their board will be glad to have hired three years from now. We agreed the engagement with the client's Chief Operating Officer, Jason Myers, and we begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}}, so before any of us picks up a phone I want the team aligned on the objective, on who owns what, and on the first moves. The mandate is a retained CFO search for a mid-market firm that is growing into a finance function it does not yet have, which means we are looking less for a careful caretaker of the books and more for an operator who can build one. This is a correspondence-heavy search by its nature, because the client is anxious to get the hire right and the best candidates are people who are not looking, so the way we keep both sides steady is by staying in close, unhurried contact with each of them.
The person we are looking for

The specification is not written yet, and settling it with Jason Myers and his board is the first real task, but the shape of the role is already clear from our conversations with the client. They want a Chief Financial Officer who has carried a company through a growth stage like the one they are in, who can stand up the reporting and controls a larger business needs, and who will be a genuine partner to a Chief Executive rather than a scorekeeper for one. Discretion matters here as it always does, so we will describe candidates to the client by their current seat and record, and we will hold names close until both sides want to meet.
How the work divides

items: Specification and calibration: I will draft the position specification and settle it with Jason Myers and the board, so that the whole team is searching against one agreed brief rather than four private ones.

Market map and long list: James Grant will lead the mapping at the senior-operator level, working the sectors where a Chief Financial Officer of this profile is actually to be found, and building the long list from that map rather than from a list we already hold.

Outreach and scheduling: Jeffrey Patterson will run the candidate threads, make the first approaches once we have agreed them, and keep every conversation moving so that no promising prospect goes quiet while we are busy elsewhere.
Engagement logistics: James Weiss is handling the paperwork, the client billing, and the meeting arrangements, so that the three of us can keep our attention on candidates and on the client.

blocks.text: First moves

Because the specification gates everything else, that is where we start. This week I will get a draft of the position specification to Jason Myers, and I would like James Grant to begin the market map in parallel so that we are not sitting idle while the client reads. Jeffrey Patterson, please set a standing weekly check-in for the three of us and a first calibration call with the client once the draft specification is in their hands. If anyone sees a reason the plan above will not hold, tell me now, so we can fix it before the search is underway.

To: Jason Myers
Cc: Jeffrey Patterson, James Grant
Hi Jason,

A short update on the CFO search before our call. The market map is nearly complete, James Grant has the long list close to closed, and Jeffrey Patterson has good first conversations going with several people whose current roles fit what {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} needs. I am keeping the whole thread orderly on our side so that nothing slips between now and when you meet a slate.

The one thing I need from you before we go further is a short read from the Roach, Moss and Hall board on two points in the specification, priorities really, so that I am not sending candidates against a brief that has quietly shifted. When the formal slate summary reaches your committee it will come under my name, Sandra Fuentes, so please route any questions on it straight to me rather than to the wider team. Ten minutes on the phone works if that is easier than writing it out.

On timing, we are comfortably inside the window we set at kickoff. Once James Grant closes the long list this week, I will send you a proposed date for the first proper review of where the field is heading, and we can fit it around your board's calendar rather than ours.
Best regards
Meeting Minutes: CFO Search for Roach, Moss and Hall

These minutes record the working session held by the search team on the Chief Financial Officer search for {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}. The session was called to review the completed market map, to agree which prospects move into first-round interviews, and to confirm what the client will see and when.
Present

items: Sandra Fuentes, Principal
James Grant, Senior Consultant
Jeffrey Patterson, Research Consultant
Jason Myers, Chief Operating Officer, Roach, Moss and Hall

blocks.text: The market map and the field

James Grant presented the completed market map. The mapping covered the sectors agreed at kickoff, the search identified a long list of prospects across them, and the team reviewed that list one segment at a time. Consistent with the firm's practice while a search is live, prospects were discussed by their current role and record rather than by name, so that nothing about a candidate's interest travels before they are ready for it to. The field is stronger in the two segments closest to the client's own sector and thinner in the third, which the team took to reflect where a Chief Financial Officer of this profile is actually to be found.

The team then worked through which prospects should move forward. The criterion applied was fit against the agreed specification rather than the length of a resume, the segment weightings were adjusted so that outreach concentrates where the field is strongest, and the thinner third segment was left open in case a late name surfaces. No prospect was set aside for any reason other than a poorer fit with the brief.

On the division of the next stage of work, James Grant, whom the team calls Jim, agreed to take the first-round interviews of the most senior prospects himself, given his experience with board-facing mandates. Jeffrey Patterson agreed to schedule those interviews and to hold the candidate threads current while the round runs, and Sandra Fuentes agreed to keep the position specification aligned with anything the client adjusts along the way.
What the client wants to see

Jason Myers set out how the Roach, Moss and Hall board wants the process to run from here. He asked that the team bring the committee a short slate rather than a long one, that each candidate be presented by evidence of what they have built rather than by biography alone, and that the board be given room to meet finalists without the timetable forcing a decision. Sandra Fuentes confirmed that the firm's approach already matches those preferences and that the client will see nothing until the field has been interviewed and tested.
Action items

rows: Begin first-round interviews with the most senior prospects on the long list and record read-outs for the team
Refine the position specification against the board's stated preferences and confirm any change with Jason Myers
Schedule the first-round interviews, keep every candidate thread current, and hold a provisional date for the next joint review
Confirm the board members who will sit on the interview panel and the window in which they can meet

blocks.text: The single item that governs the schedule from here is the first round of interviews, and every date that follows depends on when those conclude. The team will reconvene with the client once the read-outs are in hand.
Status Report: CFO Search for Roach, Moss and Hall
Prepared by Sandra Fuentes, Principal, for the hiring committee of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}.
Where the search stands

The search is on track and now at its midpoint. The field has been mapped and the first candidates interviewed, a strong group of prospects has emerged, and the work in front of us is to narrow that group to the short slate the committee will meet. We are working within the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.fee}} agreed at the outset, and the engagement remains on budget and on schedule.
What we have done this period

Since the last report the team has completed the market map and moved the search into interviews. James Grant has led the first-round interviews of the most senior prospects and recorded his read-outs for the rest of us, and his judgment has already thinned the field to the people who genuinely fit what the business needs of a Chief Financial Officer. Jeffrey Patterson has kept every candidate thread current, arranged the interviews without a single slot slipping, and stayed close to the prospects who are weighing a move so that none of them cools while we work.

Partway through the period we sat down with the committee for a joint working session to review the completed market map together, and the client used that session to sharpen two priorities in the brief, which we have since folded into how we weigh prospects. Keeping the committee this close to the work means the slate, when it lands, will hold no surprises for the people who have to act on it. The specification itself has held steady since we first agreed it, which has kept the search orderly, and we have calibrated against it at each step so that the field we are building genuinely answers the brief.

Throughout, we have held to the discretion the assignment demands. Prospective candidates have been discussed with the committee by their current role and record, none has been named in anything that circulates, and no candidate's interest in the role has traveled beyond the handful of people who need to know it. Several of the strongest prospects are in current seats they are not advertising a wish to leave, and that discretion is the only reason they are willing to talk to us at all.
What comes next

Over the coming weeks the team will complete the remaining first-round interviews, test the strongest prospects more deeply against the specification, and assemble the short slate for the committee. Each candidate on that slate will come to you described by the evidence of what they have built and by their fit with your board, and we will hold their names in confidence until both sides are ready to meet. Once the committee has met the slate, we will move to references and support you through to an offer. I will set a date for the slate review as soon as the field is firm, and I would ask the committee to hold a provisional window now, so that the timetable does not stall for want of a calendar.
Risks and how we are managing them

Two risks are worth naming, neither of them pressing. The first is timing on the candidates' side: the strongest prospects for a role like this are people who are not looking to move, and one or two may need longer to decide than a fixed schedule would like, which we are managing by keeping them warm and honest about where they stand instead of forcing a pace. The second is the depth of the field in one of the three market segments, which came in thinner than the others; we have covered it by weighting our outreach toward the two segments where a Chief Financial Officer of this profile is more likely to be found, and we do not believe it puts the quality of the slate at risk. Nothing about the engagement's cost or timeline has changed since we began, and the search remains firmly on budget.

The search is healthy, the field is real, and we are on course to bring the committee a slate it can act on with confidence. The one thing I need from you now is a provisional date to meet that slate, which I will confirm the moment the field is firm.
